Method of Attack: Injects malicious code into the IIS Failed Request Event Buffering (FREB) module (iisfreb.dll) to intercept and monitor HTTP POST requests
Executes commands sent via specially crafted HTTP requests to logon.aspx or default.aspx pages with a password parameter
Executes base64 encoded and XOR decrypted C# code in memory without touching the disk
Acts as a .NET backdoor supporting proxying and stealthy C# code execution
Uses the compromised IIS server to communicate and execute commands on other systems, potentially reaching protected internal systems
Attack Vector: Compromise of IIS server to inject code into FREB module (initial breach method unknown)
Indicators of Compromise: HTTP POST requests to logon.aspx or default.aspx with specific password and base64 parameters
Base64 encoded and XOR 0x08 decrypted XML documents containing C# code
No files or suspicious processes created (fileless backdoor behavior)
